description:
Tier 2. Encoding is the 1BRC machinery turned around: a hash table over an alloc'd [i64] mapping 4-byte windows to positions, a match-finding loop with u32 loads, and a bounded output (LZ4_compressBound(n) = n + n/255 + 16; snappy's max is 32 + n + n/6), so alloc the bound and return {out, len}. Both reference encoders are plain C at level 1 (lz4 default, snappy has one level); parity is the expectation and compression ratio must match the reference's "fast" level bit-for-bit only if the same match policy is used, otherwise report the ratio beside the speed.

Blocked by defk-n4r.6 (the hash-table pattern proven on 1BRC), defk-w38, defk-n4r.2, defk-n4r.4.

Expected verdict: parity with the NIFs, good vs any Elixir baseline (there is none worth using; write a first-pass one for the record).

Done when: the kernel's output decodes with the reference library and with the decode ticket's kernel, ratios and speeds recorded, README row added.
title: LZ4 and Snappy block encode from scratch (hash table over arrays, after 1BRC)
